# Command reference

Every `knowledge.py` command with its arguments and options, generated from the Typer app (the commands are read
off the app object, not parsed from `--help`). Prefix each command with `uv run python knowledge.py`; run
`<command> --help` for the same text in the terminal. The [README](../README.md) has the short table and the
usual workflow.

### `add-fact STATEMENT`

Append an ad hoc fact to general_facts.json (in knowledge-private), enforcing the shape seed_general_facts.py expects. Freshness is mandatory (#7). A new fact needs EITHER --recheck-by (a date or short phrase) OR --no-decay together with --recheck-rationale saying why it does not decay; neither, or both, is refused. --no-decay is NOT an excuse to default --trust to 'verified': the fact still needs an honestly considered trust level (cross-checked against an ID vs. typed from memory). The schema only enforces that one of the two is present; it cannot judge whether a fact really does not decay. Staleness only: a fact that was wrong when typed is --trust's job.

- `--allow-dirty`: Skip the clean-tree check on knowledge-private (deliberate batch edits only); the commit still contains only the facts file.
- `--applies-to APPLIES_TO`: Who or what the fact applies to (a population or condition the source states); never guess one (#45).
- `--captured-via CAPTURED_VIA`: Where the fact came from: cli, mcp, migrate-memory, ... With 'mcp', --session-id and --source-quote are required.
- `--domain DOMAIN`: Only applies if --subject doesn't exist yet.
- `--kind KIND`: What kind of assertion this is. Self-reported guidance.
- `--no-decay`: Assert this fact does not decay (a birthdate, a completed purchase); requires --recheck-rationale and excludes --recheck-by. It does NOT justify --trust verified.
- `--not-personal`: Mark as not about the user personally (default: personal).
- `--notes NOTES`
- `--origin-path ORIGIN_PATH`: The file this fact was extracted from; its SHA-256 is recorded as the fixity baseline (#38) when readable.
- `--original-claim`: This is your own conclusion, not something a source states.
- `--recheck-by RECHECK_BY`: A date (YYYY-MM-DD) or short phrase like 'next physical'. Required unless --no-decay.
- `--recheck-rationale RECHECK_RATIONALE`: Why this recheck date; with --no-decay, why the fact does not decay (required).
- `--session-id SESSION_ID`: The conversation/session the fact was captured in.
- `--source-citekey SOURCE_CITEKEY`: Must already exist in the `sources` table.
- `--source-locator SOURCE_LOCATOR`
- `--source-quote SOURCE_QUOTE`: The words that justified the fact (with --captured-via, no --source-citekey is needed).
- `--subject SUBJECT` (required): kebab-case subject name, e.g. 'car-maintenance'. Reused if it already exists, otherwise created.
- `--trust TRUST_LEVEL` (required)
- `--trust-rationale TRUST_RATIONALE`
- `--valid-from VALID_FROM`: When the fact became true: YYYY, YYYY-MM or YYYY-MM-DD (#40). Omit if unknown.
- `--valid-to VALID_TO`: When it stopped being true (same formats). Omit if still true as far as known.
- `--visibility VISIBILITY`: private (default) or normal. Only 'normal' facts may leave the local machine; when unsure, leave it private.

### `add-facts [FILE]`

Add a batch of reviewed facts from a JSON list (FILE, or - / no argument for stdin) in one atomic write and one commit. --dry-run shows each item's resulting visibility and the rule behind it.

- `--allow-dirty`: Skip the clean-tree check on knowledge-private (the commit still holds only the facts file).
- `--captured-via CAPTURED_VIA`: Provenance token, e.g. cli, mcp. With 'mcp' every item needs source_quote and --session-id is required.
- `--dry-run`: Print each item's resulting visibility and the rule behind it; write and commit nothing.
- `--json`: Machine-readable result.
- `--session-id SESSION_ID`: The conversation the facts were captured in.
- `--status STATUS`: active (default: a human reviewed them) or pending (queue for review).

### `approve [REFS...]`

Approve pending facts (REF is a fact id or a source_key): appends an 'active' revision and commits it to the data repo. Only pending facts change; others are skipped.

- `--all`: Approve every pending fact.
- `--allow-dirty`: Skip the clean-tree check on the data repo (deliberate batch edits only); the commit still contains only fact_revisions.jsonl.
- `--json`: Print machine-readable JSON instead of text.
- `--reason REASON`: Why; recorded as the revision's change_reason.

### `audit-claims`

List claims whose premises (cited facts) are superseded, retracted or past recheck_by. Exit 1 when a grounds/backing premise is stale; a stale rebuttal is listed as information only (it strengthens the claim).

- `--json`: Print machine-readable JSON instead of text.

### `audit-source-status`

List active/pending facts that cite a retracted source, one under an expression of concern, or one that was superseded (with its replacement). Exit 1 when any are found.

- `--json`: Print machine-readable JSON instead of text.

### `audit-sources`

List facts whose source file changed, went missing or moved since the fact was extracted (SHA-256 baseline). Exit 1 when any are found.

- `--json`: Print machine-readable JSON instead of text.

### `build`

Rebuild knowledge.db from schema.sql + scripts + data/.

- `--check`: Build into a throwaway file and report counts; live DB untouched.

### `build-info`

Which inputs and code produced this knowledge.db: the latest build row and its input manifest. --compare OTHER.db lists inputs that differ (exit 1 when any).

- `--compare COMPARE`: Another knowledge.db to compare input hashes against.
- `--json`: Print machine-readable JSON instead of text.

### `clean-concerts`

Clean concerts.csv in place (dedupes rows).

No options.

### `docs build`

Rewrite every generated region of README.md and docs/\*.md from the code. Hand-written text is untouched.

- `--root ROOT`: Repository root to read and write (default: this checkout).

### `docs check`

Fail (exit 1) when a generated region differs from what the code renders; writes nothing.

- `--root ROOT`: Repository root to read and write (default: this checkout).

### `edit REF`

Edit a fact by appending a revision. REF is a fact id (digits) or a source_key. Give at least one of the field options and --reason. An empty string clears --trust-rationale, --recheck-by or --notes. The subject cannot be changed and visibility is never lowered.

- `--allow-dirty`: Commit even if the private repo has other uncommitted changes.
- `--json`
- `--notes NOTES`
- `--reason REASON` (required): Why (recorded in history).
- `--recheck-by RECHECK_BY`: YYYY-MM-DD
- `--statement STATEMENT`: New statement text.
- `--trust TRUST`: New trust level.
- `--trust-rationale TRUST_RATIONALE`

### `entity add NAME`

Add an entity. Its id is derived from the name. --private makes facts that mention it private.

- `--alias ALIAS`: Another name for it (repeatable).
- `--allow-dirty`: Skip the clean-tree check on knowledge-private (the commit still holds only the files touched).
- `--dry-run`: Report what would change and commit; write nothing.
- `--external-id EXTERNAL_ID`: Optional outside identifier, e.g. wikidata:Q42.
- `--json`: Print machine-readable JSON instead of text.
- `--notes NOTES`
- `--private`: Facts that mention it become private.
- `--type TYPE`: person | organization | place | project | substance | other

### `entity alias REF ALIAS`

Add another name for an entity. Its facts are found by every name.

- `--allow-dirty`: Skip the clean-tree check on knowledge-private (the commit still holds only the files touched).
- `--dry-run`: Report what would change and commit; write nothing.
- `--json`: Print machine-readable JSON instead of text.

### `entity list`

List entities (from entities.json) with type, privacy and linked-fact counts (from the built db).

- `--json`: Print machine-readable JSON instead of text.

### `entity migrate-keywords`

Convert every privacy keyword into a private entity (type other) and clear the keyword list, in one commit. Checked first: nothing becomes less private.

- `--allow-dirty`: Skip the clean-tree check on knowledge-private (the commit still holds only the files touched).
- `--dry-run`: Report what would change and commit; write nothing.
- `--json`: Print machine-readable JSON instead of text.
- `--keep-keywords`: Only add the entities; leave the keyword list as it is.

### `entity show REF`

One entity in full. REF is its id, canonical name or an alias.

- `--json`: Print machine-readable JSON instead of text.

### `entity tag REF`

Make an entity private: every fact that mentions it becomes private (after a rebuild).

- `--allow-dirty`: Skip the clean-tree check on knowledge-private (the commit still holds only the files touched).
- `--dry-run`: Report what would change and commit; write nothing.
- `--json`: Print machine-readable JSON instead of text.

### `entity untag REF`

Make an entity non-private again. Facts already stored private stay private.

- `--allow-dirty`: Skip the clean-tree check on knowledge-private (the commit still holds only the files touched).
- `--dry-run`: Report what would change and commit; write nothing.
- `--json`: Print machine-readable JSON instead of text.

### `facts`

List/filter facts without full-text search. Active facts by default; --include-pending adds pending ones, --status X shows only status X.

- `--entity ENTITY`: Only facts that mention this entity (its id, name or an alias; #42).
- `--identifier IDENTIFIER`: Only facts that cite a source with this DOI, ISBN, ISSN, PMID, arXiv or PMC id (#48; a `doi:` style prefix is optional).
- `--include-pending`: Also show pending (unreviewed) facts; by default only active facts are listed.
- `--json`: Print machine-readable JSON instead of text.
- `--kind KIND`: Only facts of this kind: observation, measurement, decision, preference, plan, definition, inference, rule, lesson, unclassified.
- `--limit LIMIT`
- `--not-personal`
- `--personal-only`
- `--status STATUS`
- `--subject SUBJECT`
- `--trust TRUST`
- `--valid-at VALID_AT`: Only facts that were true on this date, YYYY-MM-DD (valid time, #40; not --as-of, which is when the db learned it).

### `history REF`

Every revision of a fact, oldest first. REF is a fact id (digits) or a source_key.

- `--json`: Print machine-readable JSON instead of text.

### `inbox`

Serve the pending-fact review page on 127.0.0.1 ONLY (it shows private facts; never expose it). Lists the built db snapshot: rebuild to see new pending facts.

- `--no-open`: Do not open a browser tab.
- `--port PORT`: Port on 127.0.0.1 (0 = any free port).

### `migrate-memory`

Import Claude Code memory (~/.claude/projects/\*/memory/\*.md) as private pending facts. feedback files are skipped; a second run adds nothing. Use --dry-run first.

- `--allow-dirty`: Skip the clean-tree check on knowledge-private (e.g. after a killed run); the commit still contains only the facts file.
- `--dry-run`: Report what would be written; write nothing.
- `--json`: Print machine-readable JSON instead of text.
- `--memory-root MEMORY_ROOT`: Folder holding \<project\>/memory/\*.md (default ~/.claude/projects).
- `--verbose`: Also list files already migrated.

### `privacy add-keyword KEYWORD`

Add a name/keyword; statements containing it as a whole word become private. Literal text, case-insensitive.

- `--allow-dirty`: Skip the clean-tree check on knowledge-private (deliberate batch edits only); the commit still contains only the rules file.
- `--dry-run`: Report what would change and commit; write nothing.

### `privacy check STATEMENT`

Resolve the visibility a statement would be stored with, and name the rule that raised it.

- `--json`: Print machine-readable JSON instead of text.
- `--requested REQUESTED`: What the caller asks for; default normal shows what the rules alone do.
- `--subject SUBJECT` (required): Subject the fact would be filed under.

### `privacy remove-keyword KEYWORD`

Remove a keyword. Facts already stored private stay private.

- `--allow-dirty`: Skip the clean-tree check on knowledge-private (deliberate batch edits only); the commit still contains only the rules file.
- `--dry-run`: Report what would change and commit; write nothing.

### `privacy rules`

Show the loaded privacy rules (subject tags and keywords).

- `--json`: Print machine-readable JSON instead of text.

### `privacy tag SUBJECT`

Tag a subject private (inherited by its children); --tag normal only registers it as a known subject.

- `--allow-dirty`: Skip the clean-tree check on knowledge-private (deliberate batch edits only); the commit still contains only the rules file.
- `--dry-run`: Report what would change and commit; write nothing.
- `--tag TAG`

### `privacy untag SUBJECT`

Remove a subject's tag.

- `--allow-dirty`: Skip the clean-tree check on knowledge-private (deliberate batch edits only); the commit still contains only the rules file.
- `--dry-run`: Report what would change and commit; write nothing.

### `reject REFS...`

Reject pending facts (REF is a fact id or a source_key): appends a 'retracted' revision. Only pending facts change; others are skipped.

- `--allow-dirty`: Skip the clean-tree check on the data repo (deliberate batch edits only); the commit still contains only fact_revisions.jsonl.
- `--json`: Print machine-readable JSON instead of text.
- `--reason REASON` (required): Why; recorded as the revision's change_reason.

### `retract REF`

Mark a fact retracted (appends a revision; never edits the entry).

- `--allow-dirty`: Skip the clean-tree check on knowledge-private (the commit still holds only the revision log).
- `--json`: Print machine-readable JSON instead of text.
- `--reason REASON` (required): Why (required; recorded in the revision history).

### `review-pending`

List pending (unreviewed) facts, oldest first.

- `--json`: Print machine-readable JSON instead of text.

### `search TERMS`

Full-text search over facts (statement/trust_rationale/notes).

- `--entity ENTITY`: Only facts that mention this entity (its id, name or an alias; #42).
- `--identifier IDENTIFIER`: Only facts that cite a source with this DOI, ISBN, ISSN, PMID, arXiv or PMC id (#48; a `doi:` style prefix is optional).
- `--include-pending`: Also show pending (unreviewed) facts; by default only active facts are listed.
- `--json`: Print machine-readable JSON instead of text.
- `--kind KIND`: Only facts of this kind: observation, measurement, decision, preference, plan, definition, inference, rule, lesson, unclassified.
- `--limit LIMIT`
- `--not-personal`
- `--personal-only`
- `--status STATUS`: Only facts with this status (overrides the active-only default and --include-pending).
- `--subject SUBJECT`
- `--trust TRUST`
- `--valid-at VALID_AT`: Only facts that were true on this date, YYYY-MM-DD (valid time, #40; not --as-of, which is when the db learned it).

### `set-visibility REF VISIBILITY`

Promote to normal or demote to private (appends a revision). Lowering to normal is refused when the privacy rules keep the fact private.

- `--allow-dirty`: Skip the clean-tree check on knowledge-private (the commit still holds only the revision log).
- `--json`: Print machine-readable JSON instead of text.
- `--reason REASON` (required): Why (required; recorded in the revision history).

### `show FACT_ID`

Show one fact in full, with its sources. --as-of DATE shows it as it stood then (end of that day, UTC; or an ISO timestamp).

- `--as-of AS_OF`: YYYY-MM-DD (end of that day, UTC) or an ISO-8601 timestamp.
- `--json`: Print machine-readable JSON instead of text.
- `--valid-at VALID_AT`: Also say whether the fact was true on this date, YYYY-MM-DD (valid time, #40). Exit 1 when it was not.

### `source ids CITEKEY`

Show a source's identifiers (DOI, ISBN, ISSN, PMID, arXiv, other) and any it shares with another source.

- `--json`: Print machine-readable JSON instead of text.

### `subject alias NAME ALIAS`

Give a subject another name. New facts filed under the alias are stored under the subject.

- `--allow-dirty`: Skip the clean-tree check on knowledge-private (the commit still holds only subjects.json).
- `--dry-run`: Report what would change and commit; write nothing.
- `--json`: Print machine-readable JSON instead of text.

### `subject deprecate NAME`

Refuse a subject for NEW facts (existing facts keep it); --replaced-by names the one to use instead.

- `--allow-dirty`: Skip the clean-tree check on knowledge-private (the commit still holds only subjects.json).
- `--dry-run`: Report what would change and commit; write nothing.
- `--json`: Print machine-readable JSON instead of text.
- `--replaced-by REPLACED_BY`: The subject to use instead.

### `subject describe NAME TEXT`

Set a subject's scope note (blank text clears it).

- `--allow-dirty`: Skip the clean-tree check on knowledge-private (the commit still holds only subjects.json).
- `--dry-run`: Report what would change and commit; write nothing.
- `--json`: Print machine-readable JSON instead of text.

### `subject list`

List subjects with parent, relation type, deprecation, aliases and fact counts (from the built db).

- `--json`: Print machine-readable JSON instead of text.

### `subject show NAME`

One subject in full: description, relation, aliases, children, deprecation. NAME may be an alias.

- `--json`: Print machine-readable JSON instead of text.

### `subjects`

List subjects (indented under parent) with counts of their active facts.

- `--include-pending`: Also show pending (unreviewed) facts; by default only active facts are listed.
- `--json`: Print machine-readable JSON instead of text.

### `supersede REF`

Mark a fact superseded by another (appends a revision; never edits the entry).

- `--allow-dirty`: Skip the clean-tree check on knowledge-private (the commit still holds only the revision log).
- `--by BY` (required): The replacement fact (id or source_key).
- `--json`: Print machine-readable JSON instead of text.
- `--reason REASON` (required): Why (required; recorded in the revision history).
